attempts.party: party_dark76.json (Incineroar / Urshifu-Single / Annihilape / Hydreigon / Flutter Mane / Mega Gyarados)
attempts.why: Sableye and Bronzor led. Turn 1 Sableye Protected into my Fake Out while Bronzor set Gravity and Wicked Blow took Bronzor to 59. Turn 2 my Sucker Punch failed into Bronzor's Hypnosis (status move - my misread) and Gravity Hypnosis put Incineroar to sleep; Knock Off stripped Sableye's Sash. Turn 3 the sleeper went out for Vital Spirit Annihilape and Wicked Blow killed Bronzor; Sableye's Foul Play hit Annihilape for 124 off its own Attack. Turn 4 Annihilape Protected the Will-O-Wisp and Shadow Claw while Wicked Blow killed Sableye. Turn 5 Wicked Blow one-shot Galarian Mr. Mime before its Focus Blast; a 100 BP Rage Fist killed Banette through Rocky Helmet, and Cursed Body disabled Rage Fist. Gravity expired. Turn 6 Annihilape out for Gyarados (double Intimidate) while Wicked Blow plus Life Orb recoil killed Necrozma; Photon Geyser and a -1 Band Poltergeist both landed on the incoming Gyarados and killed it - the one faint. Turn 7 Hydreigon's Dark Pulse ended Dusknoir.

protect_ledger.payoff: blocked Incineroar's Fake Out (real payoff), at the cost of not setting Prankster Gravity - Bronzor set it anyway

protect_summary: 1 Protect, real payoff. No empty guards.
ai_notes: Sensible: Sableye Foul Play targeting the highest-Attack player battler; Will-O-Wisp aimed at the non-Dark Annihilape rather than the Prankster-immune Dark types; Necrozma and Dusknoir focus-fired the same slot. Engine text note (not AI): turn 1 printed 'The opposing Bronzor couldn't fully protect itself' when Bronzor had used Gravity, not Protect, and took full damage (182); a stray Unseen Fist string, cosmetic.

level_changes.why: won attempt 1 with one faint; Sableye never set Gravity and died turn 4 after a Protect and two Foul Plays
Shadow Claw into a Protect, then one-shot; the room's cheapest body

level_change_rationale: Brief step 5: first-try win with 0-1 faints. Necrozma is the ace and untouched; the +1s go to the two offset-1 supports that contributed least.
cooler: The concept shows clearly - Gravity went up turn 1, Hypnosis landed, the grounded-for-both-sides discipline is real. It is a good room. The one weakness is that Sableye's Prankster is neutralised by any Dark-type lead (Prankster Will-O-Wisp fails into Dark types, and Fake Out beats Prankster Gravity), so the room's opener collapses into 'Bronzor sets it, slowly'. Cooler: give Sableye Fake Out or Quash of its own, or swap Sableye's Protect for Taunt so it can stop the player's own setup under the Gravity it created. Suggestion only.
legality_notes: All sets legal as authored. Dusknoir's Choice Band lock chose Poltergeist over the plan's Earthquake lane; not a defect, just the higher-value move on the board.
verification_limit: The +1 on Sableye and Banette cannot be re-verified until the main agent rebuilds.
